mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1800 units, indicating robust demand, boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST surpasses 1800 units.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.05% signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as investors seek higher yields.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 1.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) drops below 5.5% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200,000 in a month, the combined signal of a tight labor market boosts S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns over 60d are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.10) in triggered instances compared to non-triggered.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 6-month moving average, signaling supply chain resilience, leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward hit rate falls below 55% over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Real GDP (GDPC1) growth exceeding 3% on a quarterly basis, indicating strong aggregate demand, predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns over 60d are not significantly correlated (p > 0.15) with GDPC1 growth in triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within a month, signaling a rapid monetary policy response, leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days, as investors reassess economic outlook.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.5% in two consecutive months and payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth slows to less than 50,000, the combined signal of a weakening labor market leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rise > 0.5% over 2 months and PAYEMS growth < 50,000
failure_condition: SPX returns over 20d are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.12) in triggered instances compared to non-triggered.

mechanism_narrative: Retail and food services sales (RSAFS) growth below its 3-month moving average, signaling sluggish consumer spending, predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward false negative rate exceeds 40% over any 18-month rolling window.
